newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr National says knows of no sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Cr National says knows of no sale plans.

text.p: French bank Credit National said on Wednesday that it was not aware of plans by any of its long-term shareholders to sell their stakes.
"We haven't been told anything...Nothing has changed in the situation of Credit National," said spokesman Philippe Perier.
Credit National shares were up 8.07 percent at 305.40 francs at 1508 GMT, boosted by an article in the newspaper La Tribune which said the bank may be a takeover target.

Credit National chairman Emmanuel Rodocanachi said as much in an interview last month with the weekly Journal des Finances, citing the weak share price and the fact that 60 percent of the stock was widely held.

The bank's long-term shareholders own a combined 31 percent. Axa holds 9.5 percent, state-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations has seven percent, AGF has seven percent, Credit Foncier de France owns 2.5 percent and Germany's IKB holds five percent of the bank.
They have agreed to extend to one another an offer of first refusal under a long-term shareholder pact.
Insurer UAP, which has not signed the pact, holds 3.5 percent of Credit National, bringing the total held by merger partners Axa and UAP to 13 percent.
